summary: The current first mismatch is a deterministic self-description cell during the what-is/hero lookup path: C writes the comma in `human knight called wizard, chained to a heavy iron ball` at row 0, column 26, while JS leaves that cell blank. pager.c self_lookat() appends `, chained to ` plus ansimpleoname(uball) whenever Punished is true; js/pager.js:self_lookat() currently stops after the player name. The smallest scope is a divergence fix to this existing helper, using the existing ansimpleoname() implementation and state.uball. The earlier mk_knox_portal wizard-gated RNG and portal-placement findings, and the mkshop source trace, remain valid prior boundaries.

source.branch: pager.c self_lookat() builds the visible hero description from race, current monster form, and player name, then appends mounted and hidden-region details when their C predicates hold. For Punished (the uball pointer is non-null), it appends `, chained to ` followed by ansimpleoname(uball), with `nothing?` only for the impossible null-ball case. A trapped hero then receives the trap_predicament suffix. The assigned state reaches the ordinary visible human branch with Punished true, so the missing suffix is the current actionable branch.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/pager.c:657-670 lookat() calls self_lookat() when the visible glyph is the hero.
nethack-c/upstream/src/pager.c:1979-2000 look_all() calls self_lookat() for the hero in the monster listing path; nethack-c/upstream/src/pickup.c:1155-1163 also uses it for the fake hero entry.
js/pager.js:513-531 look_all() and :823-835 do_screen_description() call js self_lookat() for the hero lookup paths exercised by the port.
dependencies: nethack-c/upstream/src/pager.c:108-133 is the source function; js/pager.js:237-253 is the current implementation. Import js/objnam.js ansimpleoname() and append its result when state.uball is present, preserving the existing base description and exceptional-state guards.
nethack-c/upstream/src/objnam.c:2428-2470 defines simpleonames()/ansimpleoname(); js/objnam.js:853-876 already ports those functions and formats the attached ball name without a new random call.

nethack-c/upstream/src/youprop.h:77 defines Punished as uball != 0; js/steed.js:129-132 provides the equivalent predicate and js/detect.js:625-628 documents state.uball as the single ball-and-chain state location.

The earlier mk_knox_portal source fix at nethack-c/upstream/src/mklev.c:2643-2658 and the mkshop trace at nethack-c/upstream/src/mkroom.c:101-215 remain upstream dependencies already passed before this screen boundary; no RNG mismatch is present here.
